scope: Primary-source reviewed desktop and system software reconstructions, decompilations, and recompilations. This batch excludes games, generic reverse-engineering/decompiler toolchains, and records already present in the catalog.

projects.title: Acornsoft VIEW Word Processor Reconstruction
projects.game: Acornsoft VIEW B3.0 word processor for BBC Micro/BBC Master
projects.platform: 6502 BBC Micro/BBC Master ROM (VIEW B3.0) → symbolized assembly that rebuilds a byte-identical ROM; also a CP/M-65 adaptation and a portable C version for Unix-like systems
projects.status: The maintainer announced the decompilation and C translation as finished on 2026-10-04. The README documents a bit-identical assembler rebuild and a portable C version with most editing functions; printing, screen-mode changes, and star commands are unsupported, and the author warns that bugs may remain.
projects.summary: Reverse engineering and source reconstruction of Acornsoft VIEW, a 6502 word processor. The repository contains a symbolized assembly reconstruction that reassembles to the original B3.0 ROM, a CP/M-65 adaptation, and a portable C port branded C-VIEW B4.0. It is an application reconstruction rather than a decompiler or game project.
projects.strategy: Symbolized 6502 disassembly and byte-identical assembly rebuild, plus semantic source reconstruction into portable C and a CP/M-65 adaptation
projects.source_available: Public repository. The maintainer says their additions are CC0, but the original software's copyright owner is unknown and the repository README explicitly says the original code's legal status is unclear.
projects.subtype: Classic microcomputer productivity software / word processor

projects.title: Xbox Dashboard Build 3944 Recompiled
projects.platform: Original Xbox x86 executable (xboxdash.xbe) → native x86-64 Windows; Xbox kernel calls are mapped to Win32 and the dashboard's Direct3D 8 path is hosted through Direct3D 11
projects.status: Bring-up, not a usable dashboard yet. The maintainer reports the original initialization and XIP scene-loading paths reach the frame loop and clear a 1280×960 surface, but the command stream has zero draw calls. A flash-digest check currently makes the dashboard return to firmware; six indirect-call targets also remain unresolved. Latest code push: 2026-10-14.
projects.summary: Statically recompiles the original Xbox's build-3944 dashboard executable from x86 into C and links it to a Windows runtime for Xbox kernel, D3D8, audio, input, and NV2A behavior. This is a system application, not an Xbox game or general-purpose emulator. The project requires the user's own dashboard executable and supporting files; its current black framebuffer/zero-draw state is explicitly documented.
projects.strategy: Static x86-to-C recompilation with Xbox system-call and graphics runtime mappings
projects.source_available: Public project source and analysis metadata; the original Xbox executable/assets and generated lifted code are not distributed. The repository's MIT license applies only to project-owned code, not the original dashboard or derivative lifted code.
projects.programming_language: C and Python (with CMake build files)
projects.subtype: Console system-shell static recompilation / native Windows port

projects.title: Theseus / UIX Desktop
projects.game: Original Xbox Dashboard and its UIX desktop-shell reconstruction
projects.platform: Modded original Xbox as a drop-in dashboard replacement; Windows, macOS, and Linux desktop builds. Desktop rendering uses Metal on macOS and Vulkan on Windows/Linux through bgfx.
projects.status: The README documents a working drop-in dashboard for modded Xbox consoles and a desktop UIX application for Windows, macOS, and Linux. It describes the reconstruction as ongoing; the upstream repository is not archived, and its latest code push was 2026-08-16.
projects.summary: A reverse-engineered C++ reconstruction of the original Xbox dashboard engine, rebuilt plank by plank from retail and patched XBE behavior. On Xbox it replaces the stock dashboard; on desktop, UIX Desktop repurposes the engine as a native launcher and media center. It is distinct from Xbox Dashboard Recompiled: Theseus reconstructs shared source and UI behavior, while that project mechanically recompiles build-3944 machine code.
projects.strategy: Reverse-engineered C++ source reconstruction of the dashboard engine, with a shared Xbox target and native desktop UIX port
projects.source_available: Public source repository under GPL-3.0-or-later. The README lists third-party component licenses and documents separate build requirements for Xbox and desktop targets.
projects.subtype: Reverse-engineered system shell and cross-platform desktop launcher/media center
